evidence.text: The EPS bar is $0.03-0.05 in four estimate sources against Q3'25 actual $0.10. The company's own filings point to roughly $0.08-0.11. Underlying Q2'26 gross margin, after removing the $17.9m IEEPA refund and the $6.4m royalty-settlement release, was about 58.9% (Q1'26 58.1%), against 55.2% in Q3'25 when IEEPA tariffs were still charged. Q2'26 opex was about $69m. Management said 'we expect to be profitable each quarter' and guided platform growth every quarter. On about $170m of revenue and $72-75m of opex that gives roughly $22-28m of operating income. This sell-side has under-forecast EPS by 1.5-4x in each of the last eight quarters.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats came every quarter but were bought unevenly. Q3'25: $0.10 vs $0.04 with a revenue beat, and the stock fell 5.19% on revenue growth and holiday caution. Q2'26: $0.19 vs $0.05 including one-offs, with a revenue miss, and it rose 22.87%. Q1'26: $0.10 vs $0.057, +5.21%. Q4'25: $0.04 vs $0.03, +4.63% (baseline history; https://ca.investing.com/equities/cricut-earnings).
evidence.why_not_priced: Three Sell-rated analysts have kept EPS near $0.04 through eight beats. If the market priced a ~$0.10 quarter on a $1.25bn market cap, the sell-side targets would not sit 33% below spot and short interest would not still be ~8% of the Class A float. The stock's move since July is consistent with partial pricing, so this is filed as a lean, not a lock.
evidence.independence: The Q2 8-K release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001828962/000182896226000048/cricutq22026earningsrelease.htm) and the call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/11/cricut-crct-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/) are the same company disclosure set. The consensus figures come from separate aggregators. This is an inference from company documents, not a disclosed Q3 number.

evidence.text: Q3 products revenue has to rise about 23% q/q to meet management's 'H2 products growth' claim: Q3'25 products were $87.7m and Q2'26 were $71.3m (-22% y/y). Supporting it: Maker 5 launched 2026-09-04 at $349+ bundles with a two-week Cricut.com/Michaels exclusive and was reportedly out of stock on 2026-09-05. Management also said the Q2 Europe distribution timing gap is not a Q3 headwind. Against it: the launch gives less than one month of the quarter, there were continued promotions on Maker 4 and Joy Xtra, and accessories and materials keep eroding. Platform at about +5% adds roughly $4m. Net, total revenue lands at roughly $165-176m, inside a disputed $164-177m consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3'25 fell 5.19% when 'Q3 revenue growth disappointed' (https://www.itiger.com/news/1128325695), even with an EPS beat. Q2'26 rose 22.87% despite a 22% products decline and a revenue miss. Q4'24 rose 4.21% on a revenue miss. So the revenue line has been both punished and ignored.
evidence.why_not_priced: The revenue consensus spans 7% across sources, so no single bar is priced. If the market expected a clear products return to growth, the high-end estimates ($176.6m) would be the consensus and the sell-side would have moved off Sell after the launch. Barclays maintained Sell at $4 on 2026-09-10, after the launch.
evidence.independence: The launch stock-out report is a separate source (https://www.thecraftycatsman.com/news/cricut-maker-5-launch-2026/), and Kohl's lists Maker 5 bundles at 4.6/5 from 98 reviews (https://www.kohls.com/product/prd-8711913/cricut-maker-5-essential-bundle-cutting-machine.jsp). The management claim comes from the call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/11/cricut-crct-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). The bar is disputed, so this is capped small.

evidence.text: Paid-subscriber growth has slowed to +3% y/y (3.10m in Q2'26, +25k q/q) from +6% in Q3'25. Management pre-flagged that subscriber trends soften in Q3 on seasonality, and it is testing higher iOS pricing for new subscribers. A flat or down sequential subscriber count is likely but was already told to the market.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q3'25, subscribers were +6% but active users were flat and 90-day engaged users were -3%; the stock fell 5.19% (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/35901592/cricut-inc-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results).
evidence.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: management guided it. It is filed because a sequential decline in the paid base would be the first since the subscription tiers changed, and the stock's run since July has not been tested on a subscriber print.
evidence.independence: The Q1'26 call coverage on the pricing test (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/cricut-q1-earnings-call-highlights-234318591.html) is a separate source.

evidence.text: Margin headwinds the company itself disclosed: the Q2 10-Q says Cricut is 'beginning to experience supply-chain cost pressure related to the Middle East conflict' (fuel and petrochemical inputs; vinyl and materials are petrochemical). The call added possible gross-margin pressure from ramping AI features and a marketing ramp in H2. Existing non-IEEPA tariffs remain a headwind.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q4'25, management flagged gross-margin pressure from tariffs and promotions; the stock rose 4.63% on a small beat. Margin warnings have not been punished on recent prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is largely inside what the company told the market, and the $0.03-0.05 EPS consensus already embeds heavy margin compression. It is filed small because the magnitude of the Middle East cost pressure is not quantified anywhere.
evidence.independence: This shares the 10-Q with the EPS finding, which is already sized net of these headwinds. The transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/11/cricut-crct-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/) carries the AI and marketing comments.

evidence.text: Residual IEEPA refund flow: $1.7m of refunds booked against inventory will reach cost of revenue as that inventory sells through. A $3.5m refund receivable was open at 2026-06-30, and the CFO said 'there are still some that we're working' beyond the large majority already received. That is a small one-off tailwind to Q3 gross margin.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2'26 refund-boosted quarter rose 22.87%, but that print also carried a $17.9m refund. Here the amount is a tenth of that and has no path to guidance.
evidence.why_not_priced: Too small for aggregators to model. It is a one-off below the line the stock trades on, so it is [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: The transcript confirms the remaining refunds (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/11/cricut-crct-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Same company disclosure set.

evidence.text: On 2026-10-22 Cricut signed a new 5-year $300m senior secured multicurrency revolver with BMO, replacing the undrawn 2022 JPMorgan facility. It sets no dollar limit on dividends or buybacks while pro forma net leverage is at or below 2.5x, and allows the leverage cap to step up to 3.5x after a permitted acquisition over $75m. What the money buys: nothing visible needs funding. The company is debt-free with $267m cash and $19m securities, so this is capacity for capital return or M&A, not a ramp and not distress. The buyback authorization has only $21.6m left, and the semi-annual $0.10 dividend has historically been declared around the Q3 print.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Capital-return announcements (special dividends of $0.40 in May 2024 and $0.75 in May 2025) came with Q1 prints that rose 20.32% (May 2025). No Q3 print has carried a special dividend.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a quiet 8-K that no wire covered. If the market read it as a signal of a buyback replenishment or special dividend, it would show in previews, and none mention it. The positive read is not corroborated by any stated use, so it stays small.
evidence.independence: The dividend history (FY2025 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1828962/000182896226000010/crct-20251231.htm) shows the board's pattern but says no dividend policy is adopted. Separate document.

evidence.text: The positioning is bearish into the print. All three covering analysts rate Sell or Strong Sell, with targets $3.70-4.50 (about 33% below the $6.05 spot). Short interest is 4.41m shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, about 8% of the ~55-58m Class A float, with 7.8 days to cover. Six of the last seven prints rose, three of them by 17-23%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reactions: +22.87, +5.21, +4.63, -5.19, +16.91, +20.32, +4.21 (baseline). The only decline was a Q3 print.
evidence.why_not_priced: The short has been covering (5.71m in July to 4.41m in October) while the stock rose about 36%, so part of the fuel is spent. What remains is a 7.8-day cover on a thinly traded float against a low EPS bar. If this were fully priced, short interest would have fallen further and the sell-side would have moved targets toward spot.
evidence.independence: The analyst targets come from a separate source (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/crct/forecast/). The Class A share count comes from the 10-Q cover page and the 13G.

evidence.text: CEO Ashish Arora sold 180,000 Class A shares on 2026-10-21 to 10-23 at about $6.26-6.32 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2025-08-20, leaving 4.91m direct. Form 144s and Form 4s recur every two to four weeks from August through October, which reads as a routine plan, not a signal.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no record of this stock reacting to insider plan sales.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public on EDGAR, and a pre-scheduled plan, so it is near zero by construction.
evidence.independence: The EDGAR submissions list shows the cadence of Form 144s and Form 4s (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001828962.json).

first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest (equibles.com, FINRA settlements, https://equibles.com/stocks/din/shortinterest): 2,729,394 shares on 2026-10-15, 4.27 days to cover. That compares with 2,257,432 on 09-30, 1,843,291 on 09-15 and 1,549,589 on 08-31, so it rose about 76% into the bid. The page puts it at 21.6% of 12.66M shares outstanding; percent of free float is higher but not reported. The 10-31 settlement, the first after the bid, is not yet published. Skew: none. The front chain is unusable (ATM legs not two-sided), and put/call OI is 0.09 on only 769 contracts, so the option market makes no directional statement. Tape: +9.5% over 5 days and +18.7% over 20 days. Spot is $35.05 against the $39 non-binding bid, a roughly 10% gap. The unaffected close was $32.01 on 10-27 (Restaurant Dive) or $31.10 on 10-23 (bid letter). This is a crowded short facing a takeover floor.

evidence.text: On 2026-10-26 Arkhouse and Cobblers Cove made a non-binding offer of $39.00 cash per share: no financing condition, equity committed at signing, whole-business-securitization debt with a committed bridge, and an open door to raising the price after diligence. The board rejected it on 10-29 as 'substantially undervalued' and adopted a 10%/20% rights plan expiring 2027-10-27. On 11-02 the bidders wrote that they want to discuss the proposal and a possible higher price 'once you have announced your third quarter earnings on November 4'. Spot is $35.05, about 10% under the bid and about 9.5% over the unaffected $32.01, so the print day is the first time the board's standalone case and the bidders' next move meet in public.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior bid in the baseline's seven prints (median absolute move 3.41%, max 6.42%). The bid itself moved the stock from $32.01 (10-27 close) to about $35-36. Arkhouse's last public bid, for Macy's, ended in July 2024 when Macy's cited a lack of financing certainty, and Macy's fell sharply on that news (https://www.nbcnews.com/business/business-news/macys-ends-buyout-talks-arkhouse-brigade-months-negotiations-rcna161992). That history is the reason the stock trades 10% below $39.
evidence.why_not_priced: The bid is public and priced as a probability, not a certainty: a 10% gap to $39 on a name that has never been bid for. What is not priced is how the print shifts that probability. A soft Applebee's quarter or a cut to the low end of the EBITDA guide weakens the board's 'substantially undervalued' rejection and strengthens the bidders, who have dated their re-engagement to this release. A strong quarter lifts the standalone value. Either way the unaffected price ($31-32) is unlikely to be the anchor again within one session. If the market had priced the bid as dead, spot would sit near $32. If it had priced it as done, spot would sit near $38-39.
evidence.independence: The 8-K (Item 8.01, signed 2026-11-03) confirms the proposal and the rejection: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000049754/000119312526444401/d146714d8k.htm. Restaurant Dive (2026-10-30) covers the rights plan and Bloomberg's report that the group has economic exposure to almost 20% of shares through swaps: https://www.restaurantdive.com/news/dine-brands-poison-pill-acquisition-offer-ihop-applebees/873213/. The 13D (primary_doc) shows only about 5.7% held as shares (Cobblers 1.4% plus Arkhouse 546,700 shares), so the 20% swap figure is Bloomberg's, not a filing.

evidence.text: FINRA short interest was 2,729,394 shares on the 2026-10-15 settlement, before the bid surfaced: 21.6% of 12.66M shares outstanding and 4.27 days to cover, up from 1,549,589 on 08-31. Those shorts are now positioned against a $39 cash floor-and-ceiling story. Any print, call remark or bidder statement on 11-04 that keeps the bid alive forces further covering in a stock that trades about 650k shares a day.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior squeeze is visible in the baseline. The +9.5% five-day run-up after the 10-28 Bloomberg report is consistent with partial covering, but the 10-31 settlement that would show it is unpublished.
evidence.why_not_priced: Short interest is published with a lag. The last published number predates the bid, so how much covering has already happened is unknown. If the shorts had fully covered, the 5-day run-up would be larger and spot closer to the bid; at a 10% gap, about 2.7M shares (roughly 4 days of volume) may still be short into the print.
evidence.independence: curvedtrading carries the same 09-15 (1.8M, 5.7 days) and 09-30 (2.26M, 3.4 days) rows per the search snippet: https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/din/short-interest/. Same FINRA source, so not independent of it.

evidence.text: Applebee's faces its toughest comparison of the year in Q3: +3.1% domestic comps in Q3 2025 (company release). Brinker reported on 2026-10-28, after Dine last spoke, that Chili's, Applebee's most direct casual-dining rival, comped +10.1% with +6.4% traffic over the quarter ended 2026-09-23. Applebee's comps have gone +3.1%, +1.9%, then -1.8% (Q2 2026, traffic down), and YTD it sits near 0% against a 0-2% FY guide. A second negative Applebee's quarter is the plausible print, and the Earnings Whispers preview names it as the test.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Applebee's comps drive this stock. The 2025-08-06 print fell 6.42% and the 2026-05-06 print fell 3.52% (Applebee's +1.9% but EBITDA down). The 2026-08-05 print, Applebee's -1.8% with EPS and revenue beats and guide held, rose 2.58%, so a known-weak Applebee's comp has been looked through when the guide held.
evidence.why_not_priced: Applebee's Q3 comp has no published consensus (the preview gives none), and the peer read-through came after Dine's last update. The market has focused on the bid since 10-28, the same day Brinker reported. Had the read-through been priced, DIN would have lagged on Brinker's day; instead it rose on the bid report.
evidence.independence: Q3 2025 comparison base: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/49754/000119312525265665/d10586dex991.htm. Q2 2026 traffic decline from the 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000049754/000162828026052924/din-20260628.htm. This is a proxy: Chili's taking share is an inference, not an Applebee's number, and the broader Black Box series (separate finding) points the other way.

evidence.text: Darden's FQ1 FY27 call (2026-09-24) cited the Black Box casual-dining benchmark excluding Darden, calendar-aligned to June-August 2026, at +2.4% same-restaurant sales and -0.2% guest counts. That is a materially better industry backdrop than the traffic declines Applebee's reported for Q2, and it covers two of the three months in Dine's Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Applebee's has lagged Black Box in recent quarters (Q2 traffic down while management said only IHOP beat the benchmark), so industry strength has not reliably transmitted.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is an industry series, public since September, and no Dine-specific transmission is confirmed. It is filed small because it is the broader series the Chili's proxy has to be weighed against.
evidence.independence: The Benzinga transcript confirms the benchmark definition: https://www.benzinga.com/node/61971635. It is a proxy for Applebee's, and it includes Chili's strength, so it partly overlaps the previous finding in the opposite direction.

evidence.text: EBITDA guide arithmetic from the company's own releases. H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $105.0M ($50.8M + $54.2M) against $110.9M in H1 2025. FY2025 was $219.8M, which implies H2 2025 of $108.9M (Q3 $49.0M). The low end of the reiterated $220-230M guide therefore needs H2 2026 of about $115M, roughly +5.6% y/y after a -5.3% first half. H1 adjusted free cash flow was $3.7M against $48.7M, and Applebee's commodity inflation was running +8.2% on beef. A cut to the low end, or below it, is the likely guidance line.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-05-06 print (EBITDA $50.8M vs $54.7M, guide reiterated) fell 3.52%. The 2025-08-06 print fell 6.42%. A held guide in August bought +2.58%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The CFO already flagged 'toward the lower end', so a narrowing to about $220M is largely expected. That is why this is sized small. What is not priced is a cut below $220M. A board that has just called $39 'substantially undervalued' has an incentive not to cut, which pulls this toward zero. A bid-anchored price also mutes the reaction to a standalone guide cut.
evidence.independence: FY2025 $219.8M and the guide range: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000049754/000119312526207550/d151134dex991.htm. Q3 2025 $49.0M: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/49754/000119312525265665/d10586dex991.htm. CFO remark: https://www.webull.com.au/news-detail/15390590975501312. All are company documents; the arithmetic is mine.

evidence.text: IHOP has an easy Q3 comparison (-1.5% in Q3 2025). It comped +1.5% in Q2 2026, its third straight quarter ahead of the Black Box benchmark on sales and traffic, and on the 2026-08-05 call management said 'early Q3 trends suggest that momentum is continuing' and that the Dubai Chocolate Pancakes LTO was running above expectations. A positive IHOP comp at or above the 0-2% guide is likely and offsets part of Applebee's weakness.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-08-05 print, with IHOP +1.5% and outperforming, rose 2.58%. IHOP has been the offset that holds up the multiple when Applebee's is soft.
evidence.why_not_priced: The call commentary has been public since August. The easy comparison is arithmetic nobody needs to aggregate, but there is no consensus for IHOP comps, so the size of the beat on this line is open. First Watch, the nearest daytime peer, reported on 11-03 (after Dine last spoke): comps +1.0% with traffic -1.9%, and it raised its FY outlook. That is a mixed category read, so this finding stays small.
evidence.independence: Q3 2025 IHOP -1.5%: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/49754/000119312525265665/d10586dex991.htm. First Watch Q3 2026: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001789940/000178994026000098/exhibit991q32026.htm (a peer, mixed signal). The call transcript is shared with the EBITDA finding's CFO remark.

It is a sign against a strong skew, so it is sized small: the option market is pricing the US resi slump, and this offsets only part of that.
